records.title: Diesel Emissions Scandal (Dieselgate)
records.description: Affected TDI vehicles were equipped with emissions defeat device software that caused vehicles to produce excess NOx emissions during normal driving. VW/Audi offered buybacks and repairs. Vehicles with emissions fix may have reduced performance and fuel economy. The emissions modification replaced the DPF, DOC, and SCR catalysts.
records.solution: Check vehicle status at vwdiesellookup.com or audidiesellookup.com. Extended emissions warranty covers 10 years/120,000 miles from in-service date or 4 years/48,000 miles from fix date (whichever is longer). Warranty covers the entire long block, heads, turbo and charge system, transmission and drivetrain, entire exhaust from turbo to tailpipe, and all emissions-related components including DPF, DOC, SCR converter, and dosing injector.
symptoms: Check engine light after emissions fix

citations.title: TDIClub - What exactly does the Dieselgate Warranty cover?
IDParts Blog - Dieselgate 2015 Modifications and Warranty

communityRecommendations.content: The extended emissions warranty covers the entire long block, turbo, exhaust system (turbo to tailpipe), DPF, DOC, SCR, dosing injector, and ECU/TCU electronics. Check your VIN at audidiesellookup.com for exact coverage.

Third-party extended warranty companies may refuse coverage claiming turbo/emissions issues fall under VW's dieselgate warranty. Always check with the dealer first - many repairs are covered at no cost under the settlement warranty.
Per TDIClub forum members: after the emissions fix, monitor DPF soot levels closely using VCDS. The fix changes regen behavior and some owners report more frequent DPF clogging post-fix.
Keep all service records meticulously - dealers have denied warranty claims for lack of maintenance documentation. TDIClub members recommend documenting every oil change and service visit.
If the dealer refuses a warranty repair, escalate to Audi/VW corporate. TDIClub forums have many success stories of overturned denials when escalated properly.
Turbo gasket kit prevents boost leaks and oil seepage at the turbo flanges
Boost gauge helps monitor turbo performance and catch problems early

records.title: DQ381/DQ250 S tronic Mechatronic or Internal Transmission Fault Causing No-Drive, Jerking, or Gearbox Warning
records.description: Multiple A3/S3 owners report sudden gearbox malfunction warnings, harsh shifting, loss of drive, or the transmission becoming stuck in gear. On MQB-based A3 models with dual-clutch gearboxes, failures are commonly traced to the mechatronic unit, internal speed sensors, clutch adaptation faults, or internal transmission hardware. Audi/NHTSA documentation also shows recalls on certain newer A3/S3 vehicles for transmission-related defects that can lead to loss of motive power.
records.solution: Scan the transmission control module for stored faults and verify fluid condition, adaptation values, and clutch/mechatronic data. Depending on findings, repairs range from software update and basic settings/adaptation to mechatronic replacement or complete gearbox replacement. If the vehicle falls under an open recall or service action, Audi dealer diagnosis is important before paying out of pocket.
symptoms: Vehicle will not move in D or R

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V-213 / Audi transmission defect may cause loss of drive power (certain 2022-2024 A3/S3)
NHTSA complaints database - Audi A3 transmission complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Before authorizing a replacement gearbox, have a VW/Audi specialist perform a full DSG scan, fluid check, and clutch/mechatronic adaptation. Some cars improve after software/basic settings, but no-drive faults usually need hardware repair.
Use only the correct OEM-spec DSG fluid and filter during service; neglected fluid changes can worsen shift quality and clutch wear.

claims.content: Use only the correct OEM-spec DSG fluid and filter during service; neglected fluid changes can worsen shift quality and clutch wear.

records.title: Haldex AWD Pump/Filter Contamination Leading to Rear AWD Loss on Quattro Models
records.description: Quattro A3 and S3 models using the Haldex coupling can lose rear-wheel engagement when the pump screen clogs or the pump fails. Owners often notice front-wheel-drive behavior, traction control intervention, reduced launch performance, or AWD malfunction messages. The issue is well known on MQB AWD cars and is often linked to overdue Haldex service or contamination in the pump pickup screen.
records.solution: Scan the AWD control module, verify pump activation, and inspect/clean the Haldex pump screen and fluid condition. Many cases are resolved with Haldex fluid service and pump cleaning, while others require pump replacement if the motor has failed. After repair, perform module output tests and confirm rear torque transfer on a road test.
symptoms: Reduced traction in snow or rain

citations.title: AudiWorld and VWVortex MQB Haldex pump clog/failure owner threads
NHTSA complaints database - Audi A3 drivetrain/AWD complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Do not just change Haldex fluid; remove and inspect the pump screen because debris often remains trapped there.
Use the correct Haldex fluid and replace sealing hardware when servicing the pump.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Glass Cracking or Exploding and Sunroof Frame/Rattle Problems
records.description: Owners of A3 sedan and Sportback/e-tron variants equipped with the panoramic roof have reported spontaneous glass cracking, loud popping noises, water leaks, and persistent roof rattles. Some complaints describe the outer panel shattering without impact, creating a safety concern from falling glass and sudden driver distraction. Other cases involve frame alignment or seal issues that lead to wind noise and leaks.
records.solution: Inspect the roof glass for stress cracks, frame distortion, and evidence of impact versus spontaneous failure. Repairs typically involve replacing the glass panel and, if needed, adjusting or replacing frame/seal components. If rattles or leaks are present, drains should be checked and the roof cassette alignment verified before replacing trim pieces.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints database - Audi A3 sunroof shattering/leak complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Photograph the glass immediately and inspect for impact marks before cleanup; warranty or goodwill claims are easier when spontaneous breakage is documented.
If leaks are present, clear sunroof drains and inspect cassette alignment before replacing interior trim.

records.title: DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) Clogging
records.description: The DPF can become clogged, especially with city driving and short trips that don't allow for proper regeneration cycles. This is more common after the emissions fix was applied. A clogged DPF causes reduced power and warning lights. OEM DPF assembly part numbers: 1K0254706LX (earlier production) and 1K0254708GX (later production). Fits 2009-2014 Audi A3 TDI with CBEA/CJAA engines. DPF differential pressure sensor: available from KermaTDI for CJAA/CKRA engines.
records.solution: Allow DPF regeneration by driving at highway speeds (65+ MPH) for 15-20 minutes regularly. For forced regen via VCDS: go to adaptation, enter security code 12233, change channel 18 from 0 to 1 while maintaining highway speed. Monitor soot levels via VCDS (Particle Filter Carbon Mass). If severely clogged, professional DPF cleaning with Liqui Moly 20110 DPF Cleaning Fluid (used with 20112 DPF Cleaning Flush and 7945/7946 spray tools) can help. Note: cleaning removes soot only, not ash - ash accumulation requires DPF replacement. OEM replacement DPF often back-ordered for weeks.
symptoms: Check engine light with DPF codes

citations.title: TDIClub - Best fuel or additive to prevent DPF clogging

communityRecommendations.content: OEM DPF Assembly: VW/Audi 1K0254706LX (early) / 1K0254708GX (late). Fits CBEA and CJAA engines in Audi A3 TDI 2010-2015. Often back-ordered - check Cascade German Parts or IDParts for availability. Expect $700 core charge on new units.

Liqui Moly 20110 DPF Cleaning Fluid (1 Liter) - dissolves soot contamination in clogged DPFs without removal. Use with Liqui Moly 20112 DPF Cleaning Flush and 7945 DPF Cleaning Wand Kit. Per TDIClub: this cleans soot only, not ash. Ash cannot be regenerated and requires professional bake-out or DPF replacement.

TDIClub/MyTurboDiesel tip: Drive at steady 65 MPH highway speeds for 15+ miles to trigger natural DPF regen. The car will initiate regen within about 15 miles of steady highway driving. No additive replaces actual driving and natural regen cycles.

VCDS forced regen procedure: Go to Engine > Adaptation > enter security code 12233 > Channel 18 > change value from 0 to 1 > Save. Maintain highway speed throughout the process to keep airflow. The ECU will block regen if ash level is too high for safety.
If your A3 was built before July 2009, the catalytic converter may be welded to the DPF, affecting replacement compatibility. Verify your build date before ordering parts.

Monitor DPF health with VCDS: check 'DPF Oil Ash Volume' and 'Particle Filter Carbon Mass' (spec vs actual). If ash volume is dangerously high, the ECU will not allow forced regen. At that point, DPF replacement or professional ash cleaning (bake-out) is required.

records.title: EGR Valve/Cooler Failure
records.description: The EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) valve and cooler can fail from carbon buildup, causing rough running, poor performance, and warning lights. OEM EGR valve: 03L131501K (Pierburg, supersedes 03L131501G). OEM EGR cooler: 03L131512AF (Genuine Audi). EGR cooler valve: 03L131501F. EGR pipe to cooler: 03G131547H. EGR cooler temperature sensor: 03L906529A. EGR vacuum solenoid (N239/N345): 1K0906283A. EGR to intake manifold O-ring seal: 03G131547C.
records.solution: Clean or replace EGR valve (03L131501K). Inspect EGR cooler (03L131512AF) for leaks - coolant loss can indicate internal cooler failure. Regular intake cleaning helps prevent carbon buildup. Use quality diesel fuel. The EGR cooler removal process is documented at myturbodiesel.com for CBEA/CJAA engines.

citations.title: MyTurboDiesel - EGR Cooler Removal on CBEA/CJAA

communityRecommendations.content: OEM EGR Valve: Pierburg 03L131501K (supersedes 03L131501G/D/E). Fits CBEA and CJAA engines. Available from KermaTDI, IDParts, ShopDAP. This is the valve that controls exhaust gas recirculation and commonly fails from carbon buildup.

OEM EGR Cooler: Genuine Audi/VW 03L131512AF. Fits Audi A3 2010-2013 with 2.0L TDI CBEA engine. Available from FCP Euro (lifetime warranty), ECS Tuning, and IDParts. Check for coolant leaks as primary failure mode.
EGR Cooler Temperature Sensor: 03L906529A. This sensor monitors EGR cooler outlet temperature and can trigger fault codes when failed. Replace when servicing the EGR cooler.
EGR Pipe to EGR Cooler: 03G131547H. Connects the EGR valve to the cooler. O-ring seal for EGR valve to intake manifold: 03G131547C. Replace seals whenever removing EGR components.

TDIClub community tip: Regular highway driving helps reduce carbon buildup in the EGR system. Short-trip city driving accelerates carbon accumulation. If the EGR cooler leaks internally, you may notice unexplained coolant loss without visible external leaks.

When replacing the EGR cooler, also replace the EGR cooler valve (03L131501F) and the pipe-to-cooler gasket. MyTurboDiesel.com has a detailed CBEA/CJAA EGR cooler removal guide with step-by-step photos.
EGR cooler failure can cause coolant to enter the exhaust system, leading to white smoke and potentially damaging the DPF. Address coolant loss promptly to avoid cascading damage.

records.title: Glow Plug Failure
records.description: Glow plugs can fail, making cold starting difficult, especially in cold weather. The CBEA/CJAA engines use 'smart' glow plugs with integrated cylinder pressure sensors. OEM glow plug: 03L905061F (superseded to 03L905061K, then 03L905061M, current: 03L905061L). 4 plugs per engine. Glow plug control module (J179): 03L907281 (superseded to 03L907281B). Failed glow plugs can break during removal, requiring special extraction.
records.solution: Test glow plugs with VCDS if cold start issues occur - each plug can be tested individually. Replace failed glow plugs carefully - they can seize in the head. Soak with penetrating oil before removal. Use anti-seize on new plugs. Glow plug connector wiring (04L971785C) often breaks during service and should be kept on hand. Replace glow plug control module (03L907281) if faulty.

communityRecommendations.content: OEM Glow Plug with Integrated Pressure Sensor: VW/Audi 03L905061L (current part number, supersedes 03L905061F > 03L905061K > 03L905061M). Genuine VW/Audi part. 4 required per engine. These are 'smart' glow plugs with built-in cylinder pressure sensors unique to the common-rail TDI platform. Available from FCP Euro, IDParts, UroTuning, and Cascade German Parts.

Glow Plug Control Module (Relay J179): 03L907281 (superseded to 03L907281B). Controls glow plug operation timing for optimal combustion. When this module fails, all four glow plugs stop functioning. Available from ECS Tuning, Pelican Parts, and Modded Euros.

Glow Plug Connector/Wiring Harness: 04L971785C / 04L971781C. The connector for the sensor-type glow plugs. These are fragile and frequently break during glow plug removal. Always have spares on hand before starting the job.

VWVortex/TDIClub tip: Soak glow plugs with penetrating oil (PB Blaster or Kroil) for 24+ hours before attempting removal, especially on high-mileage engines. Run the engine warm before removal to help loosen carbon deposits. Remove plugs while engine is still warm.

These glow plugs can seize and break off in the cylinder head, requiring expensive extraction (drilling/tapping). If a plug will not come out with moderate force after soaking, stop and seek a TDI specialist. Forcing a seized plug can break it, turning a $150 job into a $1000+ head repair.

Apply a thin coat of anti-seize compound (Loctite or Permatex nickel-based) to the threads of new glow plugs before installation. This prevents future seizure. Torque to spec (15 Nm) - do not overtighten.

records.title: Diesel Injector Failure
records.description: The Bosch piezo common-rail diesel injectors can fail or develop deposits, causing rough running, misfires, and poor fuel economy. Injector seals can also leak. OEM injector: VW/Audi 03L130277 (also 03L130277A), Bosch reference 0445116030. These are Bosch piezo-type injectors used across CBEA and CJAA engine codes. 4 injectors per engine.
records.solution: Use quality diesel fuel. Have injectors tested with VCDS if symptoms appear - check injection quantity deviation. Replace failed injectors individually (03L130277A, Bosch 0445116030). Always replace injector seals when removing injectors. Injector seal kit includes copper washer (WHT000884 bottom O-ring, 059130119 top O-ring, 059130519 seal ring). Consider professional injector cleaning service before full replacement.
symptoms: Diesel fuel smell around engine (injector seal leak)

citations.title: HansAutoParts - VW Audi Common Rail Diesel Injector CJAA CBEA

communityRecommendations.content: OEM Diesel Injector: VW/Audi 03L130277A (Bosch 0445116030, cross-reference 0986435360). Bosch piezo-type common-rail injector for CBEA and CJAA engines. Available from KermaTDI, HansAutoParts, and IDParts. 4 required per engine. Remanufactured injectors available at lower cost.

Injector Seal Kit (per injector): Includes bottom O-ring (WHT000884), top O-ring (059130119), and copper seal ring (059130519). Elring brand seal kit also available under part 03L130277 reference. Always replace all three seals when removing any injector.
Glow plug connector for sensor plugs (needed during injector service): 04L971785C / 04L971781C. These connectors can break during injector removal and should be kept on hand.

TDI community tip: Use VCDS to check injector quantity deviation (injection quantity adjustment values) before replacing injectors. Values outside +/- 4 mg/stroke indicate a failing injector. This test can identify the specific failed injector without guessing.

When replacing injectors, always use new copper crush washers and O-ring seals. Reusing old seals is the most common cause of post-repair fuel leaks. Apply a thin film of clean diesel fuel to the new O-rings before installation.

Injector removal on high-mileage TDI engines can be extremely difficult due to carbon seizure. Soaking with penetrating oil for 24+ hours before removal is recommended. Broken injectors require expensive extraction. Consider a TDI specialist for this job.

records.title: Turbocharger Failure
records.description: The BorgWarner BV43 variable-geometry turbocharger (OEM part 03L253056, BorgWarner 53039880208) can fail due to oil starvation, bearing wear, or variable geometry vane sticking/seizing. The most common failure mode is the variable vanes sticking or seizing, causing overboost or underboost. Catastrophic failures (compressor shaft snapping) are less common but documented. Failures typically occur around 100,000-150,000 miles.
records.solution: Regular oil changes with VW 507.00 spec diesel oil are critical - the turbo depends on clean oil for bearing lubrication. Replace turbo if failed using OEM BorgWarner unit (03L253056). Always replace the turbo oil feed line (03L145771) and oil return line (03G145736F) with new gaskets (03L145757Q oil return gasket) when replacing the turbo. Let engine idle 30-60 seconds before shutdown to allow turbo to cool down.
symptoms: Check engine light with boost codes

communityRecommendations.content: OEM Turbocharger: BorgWarner BV43, VW/Audi part 03L253056 (BorgWarner 53039880208). Brand new genuine BorgWarner unit with exhaust manifold. Fits all CBEA and CJAA 2.0L common-rail TDI engines. Available from FCP Euro (lifetime warranty), IDParts, UroTuning, and EuropaParts. Remanufactured units also available from TurbochargersDirect.

Turbo Oil Feed Line: 03L145771. Must be replaced when installing a new turbo - the banjo bolt screen can become clogged with debris, causing oil starvation to the new turbo. Available from KermaTDI and IDParts.
Turbo Oil Return Line: 03G145736F. Oil Return Line Gasket: 03L145757Q (Elring 01259800). Replace both when servicing the turbo. Old gaskets can leak and cause oil loss.

Hybrid Turbo Upgrade: Cascade German Parts and MuchBoost offer hybrid turbo upgrades for the CBEA/CJAA BorgWarner platform. These use larger compressor wheels within the stock housing for improved performance with a tune.

The most common turbo failure mode on the 2.0 TDI is variable geometry vanes sticking or seizing from carbon/soot buildup, causing overboost shutdowns. Regular highway driving and proper DPF regen cycles help keep vanes clean. Use VW 507.00 spec oil only.

ALWAYS replace the turbo oil feed line (03L145771) when installing a new turbo. Reusing the old feed line is the #1 cause of premature turbo failure after replacement - the internal screen can be clogged with debris that starves the new turbo of oil.

Before replacing the turbo, check the turbo actuator first - a failed actuator can mimic turbo failure symptoms (underboost, limp mode) and costs far less to replace. The actuator and pressure sensor can be tested with VCDS.

records.title: Virtual Cockpit/MMI Display Freezing, Rebooting, or Going Blank
records.description: Owners report intermittent failures of the digital instrument cluster or MMI system, including black screens, frozen navigation/audio, repeated reboots, and loss of backup camera or driver information display. These issues appear on both late 8V and newer 8Y cars and are often tied to software faults, control module glitches, or infotainment hardware problems. While not always immobilizing, the failure can remove speed/navigation/camera information and create significant driver frustration.
records.solution: Check for software updates, fault codes in the infotainment and gateway modules, and battery voltage stability. Some vehicles are fixed with MMI or cluster software updates and module resets, while persistent cases may require replacement of the display, MIB unit, or related control module. If the backup camera or safety features are affected, document the condition for dealer escalation.
symptoms: Loss of navigation or audio controls

citations.title: NHTSA complaints database - Audi A3 electrical/infotainment complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Before replacing hardware, verify battery health and charging voltage; low system voltage can trigger repeated MMI and cluster glitches.
Ask the dealer to check for the latest MMI/software campaigns before approving expensive module replacement.

records.title: Water Pump/Thermostat Housing Coolant Leaks on EA888 Gasoline Engines
records.description: A very common MQB Audi issue is coolant leakage from the integrated water pump/thermostat housing assembly on EA888 gasoline engines used in the A3 and S3. Owners report gradual coolant loss, sweet smell, visible residue around the pump housing, and in some cases overheating warnings. The failure is typically due to seepage or cracking of the plastic housing and seals rather than a simple hose leak.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the water pump/thermostat module beneath the intake area for pink/white residue or active seepage. The standard repair is replacement of the complete pump/thermostat assembly with updated seals, followed by proper vacuum fill and bleeding. If overheating occurred, inspect for secondary damage and verify radiator fan operation.
symptoms: Pink or white residue near water pump housing
Slow coolant loss with no obvious puddle

citations.title: NHTSA complaints database - Audi A3 cooling system/water pump complaints

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for the complete water pump/thermostat module replacement rather than piecemeal seal swapping if the housing is already leaking.
Use the correct VW/Audi coolant only and vacuum-fill the system to avoid trapped air after repair.
